title: Open DS grammar
description: The finite set of questions every Open DS scheme answers: reasons first, then scopes, plus the situations that usage rules answer and the shared component API. Written so an agent can read it cold.

scheme_order.description: The order schemes are listed in everywhere: the CLI, the MCP server, the docs, Storybook and the website. A scheme missing from the list comes after it, by id.

why.description: Why this order, in one or two sentences.

id.description: Fixed id of the grammar.

status.description: draft: the questions may still change; curated: reviewed and settled.

description.description: What the grammar is and how its parts relate.

ai.description: Guidance for an agent that reads this file.

use_when.description: When an agent should read the grammar.

how_to_read.description: How to follow answers, because links and tokens.

layers.description: The four layers of the grammar, in order.

id.description: Layer id.

description.description: What the layer holds.

methods.description: The five method questions every scope answers, in order: roles, how many, how defined, values, lands in.

id.description: Method id. Scope question ids end with it, for example typography.values.

title.description: The method as shown to people, for example How many.

description.description: What the method asks of every scope.

reasons.description: Reason groups: why the system exists. Answered before any scope.

scopes.description: Scopes: the design decisions, voice and tone included. Every scope answers the five method questions and lists the tokens it owns, the components it lands in and its situations.

situations.description: Moments where people need to know which decision or component to use. Every scheme answers each one.

id.description: Stable situation id. Machine use only; pages show the title.

scope.description: The scope the situation belongs to. Every situation belongs to exactly one scope.

title.description: The situation in plain words, as shown to people.

lead.description: How a rule about this situation opens in a sentence, when "For a {title}" does not read. For example "When someone asks for less motion".
examples: When someone asks for less motion

description.description: One sentence that defines the situation for an agent.

components.description: Components and the keys each one reads.

id.description: Component group id.

description.description: What the component does.

keys.description: Component key ids the component reads.

component_keys.description: The shared component API. Every scheme defines a value for every key.

id.description: Key id: component / part / property, and the key's token path. A part with variants has a base, @, beside them (button/primary/background/@ and button/primary/background/hover). Becomes the CSS variable --component-part-property, with the @ dropped: --button-primary-background.

component.description: The component group that owns the key.

description.description: What the key controls.

default.description: The semantic token path the key points to by default.

replaced_by.description: A deprecated key: the key that replaces it. It stays one minor release as an alias of that key (OD-241).

semantics.description: What each semantic key is for, written once for every scheme: intent, use, misuse with what to use instead, and the fills it may sit on with the contrast it must keep. Words only; values come from each scheme. The harness checks every rule.

description.description: What this list is and how to read it.

connections.description: How the tokens of a scope connect (OD-304): comes-from, pairs-with and stays-apart. The harness checks each one.

description.description: What the list holds.

items.description: One entry for each connection.
One connection between tokens.

id.description: The connection's id.

tokens.description: The tokens the connection holds for; * stands for one segment. For order, lowest first.

from.description: comes-from: the token or pattern the value comes from (@ is the token's own @). stays-apart: the tokens it stays apart from.

match.description: comes-from: hue means the same hue scale; chain means the value reads the from token on its way; scale means a type size is base × ratio^step of the scheme's type record; line-kind means a line height is the ratio of its role's line kind.

steps.description: comes-from: how many steps on from its source it sits.

pairs.description: pairs-with: the grammar list that names the pairs.

promise.description: pairs-with: the step promise. Steps this far apart give at least this contrast.

items.description: One step distance and the contrast it promises.

apart.description: The distance between two step numbers.

contrast.description: The WCAG contrast ratio the distance promises.

by.description: stays-apart: hue means no shared hue scale; delta-e means a color difference; order means a lightness order; ratio-step means a text size is at least one ratio step above the size on the step below; kind-gap means the line kinds keep min_apart between their ratios. pairs-with: holds-line means each from box is at least the line height of the tokens' role.

min_delta_e.description: stays-apart by delta-e: the smallest color difference, ΔE in OKLab ×100.

min_apart.description: stays-apart by kind-gap: the smallest gap between two line kind ratios.

modes.description: The modes the connection holds in. All modes when left out.

also.description: pairs-with: fills that hold a text but state no tone, each with the text that sits on it.

items.description: Fills and the one text that sits on them.

fills.description: The fills; * stands for one segment.

text.description: The text token that sits on each fill. Its pair contrast is the floor.

says.description: Why this text sits on these fills.

neutral.description: The neutral scale and the menu of grays it can point at (OD-228).

description.description: How the neutral scale works.

floor.description: The optional step below 0 that a scheme adds when its dark canvas sits on step 0, so dark wells sit below the page.

step.description: The step's name in color.neutral and in the gray's dark ramp.

description.description: What the floor is for, how it is derived, and what it names in light.

id.description: The primitive's hue name.

description.description: What it looks like and what it suits.

tones.description: How foregrounds pair with fills (OD-222). Each fill states its tone, light or dark, per brand and mode. What sits on it comes from color.on-light or color.on-dark.

description.description: How the tones work.

sets.description: The roles in each tone set, with the contrast each keeps on a fill that carries it.

contrast.description: The WCAG minimum on a fill.

fills.description: Every fill that carries foregrounds, and which roles it carries.

id.description: The fill's semantic path.

carries.description: The roles that sit on it.

key_colors.description: The few colors that show a theme at a glance, listed on each scheme's Themes page (OD-223).

description.description: Why these colors, in one sentence.

tokens.description: The tokens, in the order the table lists them.

items.description: A semantic token path, for example color.action.primary.@.

urgency.description: The order of status colors from least to most urgent.

description.description: The rule, for an agent: pick the level that matches the real risk.

items.description: A semantic token path, for example color.status.danger.@.

order.description: Status keys from least to most urgent.

items.description: Guidance for one semantic key.

id.description: A semantic token path, for example color.status.danger.@.

intent.description: What the key is for, in one or two plain sentences.

use_for.description: Concrete uses, for example 'Error text and icons'.

items.description: A misuse and the key to use instead.

when.description: The situation this key is wrong for.

use.description: The semantic key to use instead. It must exist.

not_for.description: Misuses, each with the key to use instead.

pairs.description: The fills this key may sit on, and the contrast it must keep on each in every brand and mode. A key in a tone set says tone: true instead of listing fills: it sits on every fill of its tone that carries its role (semantics.tones).

tone.description: The fills come from the tones: every fill whose tone matches and that carries this role.

items.description: A semantic token path, for example color.status.danger.@.

on.description: Fill keys this key may sit on.

contrast.description: The WCAG minimum: 4.5 for text, 3 for graphics and control edges, null when exempt.

order.description: Place on the urgency order, for status keys.

exempt.description: Why this key has no contrast minimum, when contrast is null.

variants.description: The meaning of each semantic name ending, such as subtle (OD-303).

description.description: What the list holds, in one sentence.

id.description: The last part of a semantic name, such as subtle or @.

says.description: What the part means, in plain words. The token map shows it.

step.description: The step of its hue scale the part sits at, such as 600 (OD-304).

from.description: The part this one moves from, such as @ for hover (OD-304).

steps.description: How many steps on from the from part it sits (OD-304).

items.description: One name ending and its meaning.
One entry for each name ending.

groups.description: The meaning of each group of a semantic name, such as color.category (OD-303).

description.description: What the list holds, in one sentence.

id.description: A group of a semantic name, such as color.category.

says.description: What the part means, in plain words. The token map shows it.

items.description: One name group and its meaning.
One entry for each name group.

reason_form.description: The form every reason takes (OD-294). The harness check reasons-say-why counts the reasons that miss a part, per scheme, and the count may only go down.

description.description: What the form is for.

form.description: The form, with each part in angle brackets.

from_above.description: How a reason for a value set from above (a scale, a relation, inheritance) fills the form.

parts.description: The parts a reason must have, each found by its marker words.

id.description: The part's id, for example job.

marker.description: The words that open the part, for example in order to.

trace.description: The trace rules: for one kind of semantic token, the grammar questions whose answers decide it. The trace engine (cli/src/trace.mjs) links every value it names to those answers, so no value rests on no decision. A rule names one kind of token, never a whole scope.

tokens.description: The tokens the rule names. The first rule that names a token is the one that applies.

items.description: A token name; * stands for one segment, for example type.*.font-size.

follows.description: The questions whose answers decide these tokens.

items.description: A grammar question id, for example typography.values.

says.description: Why each question decides these tokens, in plain words.

catalogue.description: Every component a design system can carry. Each scheme picks its inventory from these items through the components scope.

description.description: What the catalogue is and where it comes from.

families.description: Component families. The components.roles options name them.

id.description: Family id.

description.description: What components in the family do.

roles.description: For each components.roles option id, the family ids it admits, plus a description.

description.description: What the map is.

items.description: One entry per component.

id.description: Component id, as in the source registry.

description.description: What the component is for, in one sentence.

overview.description: The reference: what the component is, in one sentence, the same in every design system.

apply_when.description: The reference: when this component is the right choice.

not_when.description: The reference: when it is the wrong choice. Name what to use instead in vs.

vs.description: Components people confuse with this one, and when to use them instead.

id.description: A catalogue item id, or a pattern outside the catalogue when outside is true.

why.description: When to use that one instead.

outside.description: True when the alternative is not a catalogue component (for example a plain link).

variants.description: The reference for each variant, by axis. The axes and ids are the built component's own props (for example variant and size); state covers the states the component draws, such as hover, focus and disabled. Every scheme that carries the component decides each one.

items.description: One variant on this axis.

id.description: Id, unique in its list.

overview.description: What it is, in one sentence.

apply_when.description: When it is the right choice.

not_when.description: When it is the wrong choice, and what that case needs instead.

situations.description: The grammar situations this component serves. Each scheme's usage rule for the situation says how.

items.description: A grammar situation id.

accessibility.description: What every use of this component must do for assistive tech.

items.description: One accessibility rule.

id.description: Id, unique in its list.

overview.description: What it is, in one sentence.

apply_when.description: When it is the right choice.

not_when.description: When it is the wrong choice, and what that case needs instead.

keyboard.description: How the component works from the keyboard.

items.description: One keyboard rule.

id.description: Id, unique in its list.

overview.description: What it is, in one sentence.

apply_when.description: When it is the right choice.

not_when.description: When it is the wrong choice, and what that case needs instead.

source.description: Where the reference text comes from.

name.description: The source, for example Open UX, or Open DS when written here.

id.description: The record id in the source.

anatomy.description: The component's parts (OD-229): the drawing, every part with its roles, and the cards that follow each decision to its part. Its Anatomy reference page is generated from it.

options.description: Rules every scheme's primitives (the options) follow, so each option looks clearly different from the others. The harness checks them and the agent context carries them.

description.description: What the rules are for.

used.description: Only the options something reads (OD-222): every primitive outside the listed groups is read by a semantic, a theme, a component key or another primitive.

say.description: The rule in a few words, for the agent context.

except.description: Primitive groups kept whole even where a step is unused, such as color ramps.

rules.description: One rule per kind of option.

id.description: The kind of option.

applies_to.description: The primitive group the rule covers, as a dotted path.

type.description: The DTCG type every step must have, when the rule fixes one.

min_gap.description: The smallest difference allowed between two steps.

say.description: The rule in a few words, for the agent context.

anatomy.description: The parts layer (OD-229): the roles a part can play, as the questions they answer.

description.description: What the parts layer is, for an agent.

id.description: The role's id, which parts and cards cite.

label.description: The role's name, as the page shows it.

ask.description: The question the role answers for a person.

roles.description: The jobs a part can do for a person.

mapping.description: The decision mapping (OD-303): each design property, the question that decides it, the semantic tokens it lives in and its jobs. A reason cites its token's deciding question from here; a token with no entry is untraced.

title.description: The property's name in plain words.

scope.description: The scope the property belongs to.

question.description: The grammar question whose answer decides this property.

tokens.description: The semantic tokens the property lives in; * stands for one segment. Empty when no token carries it yet.

rule.description: The rule that makes the property's value, in plain words, such as size = base × ratio^step. The token map shows it as the token's rule.

id.description: The job id, unique in its property, such as group-and-separate.

title.description: The job in a few plain words. The token map shows it.

how.description: The relation or theory behind the job.

also.description: Other names the research gives the same job.

roles.description: The roles this property serves (OD-304), in color and type, each with the parts of the reason form: role, job, how (from the job), what people get.

items.description: One role and the tokens that play it.

id.description: The role's id, unique in the grammar.

role.description: The role in words, for 'We use <value> for <role>'.

tokens.description: The semantic tokens that play the role; * stands for one segment.

jobs.description: The ids of the entry's jobs this role does. The first job gives the 'how'; a job named after a line kind (tight, snug, open) applies only to a token of that kind.

to.description: The job as a verb phrase, for 'in order to <job>'.

gets.description: What people get, for 'So <what people get>'.

always_on.description: Marks a role that every scheme ships, whatever it answers. No option creates it; the answers in shaped_by shape it.

why.description: Why every scheme ships the role, as a clause that follows 'because'.

shaped_by.description: The question ids whose answers shape the role. The reason cites these answers.

question.description: A reason question with its possible answers.

id.description: Stable question id.

description.description: What the question decides, for a person or an agent.

options.description: The possible answers. Answers are semantic words, never raw values.

considers.description: What every answer must weigh (OD-245). Each scheme's answer says, for each one, how its choice meets it.

id.description: The consideration's id, which an answer's considers map uses as its key.

group.description: The family it belongs to, for reading it in groups.

label.description: The consideration's name, as the decision reference shows it.

ask.description: The question to answer for this consideration.

id.description: Stable option id.

description.description: What the option means when the label alone is not enough, for example the range a count word stands for.

creates.description: The color roles this option brings, by role id (OD-304). An empty list means the option shapes roles but brings none.

reason.description: A reason group with its questions. Reason question ids look like people.q1.

id.description: Group id; prefixes its question ids.

description.description: What the group decides.

scope.description: A scope: five method questions and the same parts as every other scope.

id.description: Group id; prefixes its question ids.

description.description: What the group decides.

questions.description: Exactly one question per method, in method order.

owns.description: Token paths this scope decides, for example type or size.icon. Every path exists in each scheme's tokens.

lands_in.description: Grammar component ids whose keys or words this scope sets.

situations.description: Situation ids that belong to this scope. Each scheme answers them with a usage rule.

use_cases.description: The spacing scope only (OD-294): the words that name a space token's use case. Every scheme's spacing record uses these words.

description.description: What a use case is and how a scheme uses the words.

level.description: Where the space sits: inside one component or between components.

relation.description: What the space does: separate parts, or pad a box around things.

reach.description: Which way the space runs: along one line or between blocks.

jobs.description: The spacing scope only (OD-294): the job of each spacing property and how the property does it. A token can serve more than one job; its reason names the first job that names it.

items.description: One spacing property, its job and how it does the job.

id.description: The property id, for example gap.

items.description: A token name; * stands for one segment.

property.description: The property's name as a reason says it, for example Distance.

job.description: The job the property serves, as a reason names it after in order to.

how.description: How the property does the job, as a reason says it after does this by.

properties.description: The design properties this scope's tokens carry (OD-294), for example a corner or a shadow: the jobs each property does and how it does each. Every reason for one of its tokens names one of these jobs.

items.description: One property: the tokens that carry it, how it works and its jobs.

id.description: A short id, for example corner.

title.description: The property's name in plain words.

description.description: What the property is, for a person or an agent.

items.description: A token name; * stands for one segment.

tokens.description: The semantic tokens that carry this property.

works_by.description: How the property works in general, for example the curvature of the edge.

jobs.description: The jobs the property does. A reason names its job by the job's id.

id.description: The job in one word, as reasons name it, for example nesting.

description.description: What the job is.

how.description: How the property does this job.

source.description: Where the job comes from: research, a standard, or a brand convention named as one.

relations.description: How each of this scope's tokens is set (OD-294): decided by answers, or derived from other tokens by a relation. Each scheme records which relation each token follows (scheme.relations), and cli/src/shape-elevation.mjs checks the record against the values.

id.description: The relation's id; scheme records name it.

items.description: A semantic token name.

tokens.description: The tokens this relation sets. Every scheme records each of them.

check.description: How the checker verifies it. decided: set by answers. minus: the record's from less its minus. equal-unless-pill: equals from, or the record's box corner when from is a pill. equal-or-own: equals from, unless own_when gives it its own value. next-step: the next primitive step above from. fixed: always equals. layer-step: a shadow by layer, from by_answer and steps. dark-same-shape: the dark shadow keeps the light shape.

items.description: A grammar question id.

follows.description: The answers that decide the tokens, directly or through the tokens they derive from.

items.description: A job id from the scope's properties.

jobs.description: The jobs of the property these tokens do.

count.description: For a decided token: a count answer that names how many sizes a set of tokens makes.

question.description: The count question, for example shape.count.

items.description: A semantic token name.

tokens.description: The tokens whose distinct sizes are counted.

options.description: Each answer option and the number of sizes it names.

own_when.description: For equal-or-own: the answers that give the token a value of its own.

question.description: A grammar question id, for example shape.roles.

items.description: An option id.

options.description: The options that give the token its own value.

equals.description: For fixed: the value the token always has, for example 2px.

items.description: A component token path, for example component.tabs.list.border.

boundaries.description: For a line: the component colors whose edge is the only cue that you can click or type there (the edge rule). Each reads color.border.strong and needs the floor's contrast against surface.default (WCAG 1.4.11).

floor.description: For boundaries: the contrast floor, for example 3.

depth.description: For dark-same-shape: the surfaces that show height by tone in dark mode. A raised surface lighter than the base, and a sunken one darker, read as higher and lower; anything else is a finding.

raised.description: The raised surface, for example color.surface.raised.

base.description: The base surface, for example color.surface.default.

sunken.description: The sunken surface, for example color.surface.sunken.

ring.description: The 1px ring of a raised layer, for example color.border.raised. In dark it is a solid color, lighter than the raised surface (OD-297).

items.description: A shadow token, for example elevation.overlay.

floating.description: For dark-same-shape: the layers that float (menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts, tooltips). Only these cast a shade in dark; every other layer casts none there (OD-297).

by_answer.description: For layer-step: which layers rise under each answer.

question.description: A grammar question id, for example elevation.roles.

items.description: A token name.

options.description: Each option and the tokens that cast a shadow under it.

steps.description: For layer-step: each layer's step on the scale. A higher step never casts a smaller offset or blur.

quiet.description: For a line: the component colors whose edge is not the only cue, so they stay faint (color.border.default), each with its reason.

items.description: One faint line and why it may stay faint.

token.description: A component token path, for example component.tabs.list.border.

why.description: What else shows that the part can be clicked or typed in, or why it cannot.

families.description: The motion scope only (OD-297): the motion families, the move types and the curve kinds. A scheme's family follows one answer; each family limits each duration and allows curve kinds per move. cli/src/motion.mjs checks every scheme.

description.description: What the families are and how a scheme gets one.

question.description: The grammar question whose answer picks the family, for example motion.roles.

by_option.description: Each option of the question and the family it picks.

moves.description: The move types. Each has one easing token in every scheme.

id.description: The move type, for example exit.

token.description: The easing token of this move.

description.description: When the move happens.

curves.description: The curve kinds a family can allow, each measured from the cubic Bézier.

id.description: The curve kind; cli/src/motion.mjs measures it.

says.description: How the kind is measured, in plain words.

items.description: The families.

id.description: The family id, for example productive.

description.description: What the family is for and its limits, in plain words.

additionalProperties.description: The longest the duration may take, in milliseconds.

max_ms.description: Duration token patterns and their limit; the first pattern that names a token applies.

items.description: A curve kind.

additionalProperties.description: The curve kinds this move may take.

curves.description: Each move type and the curve kinds it allows in this family.

hints.description: Rules of thumb this scope's decisions taught (OD-230): hints for the next decision, for people and agents.

id.description: A short id, for example adjust-where-measured.

measure.description: What to measure, when the hint can be measured; the harness checks the measured ones.

items.description: A ticket key.

from.description: The decisions the hint came from.

use-case-axis.description: One axis of a spacing use case: its words, each with what it means.

description.description: What the axis says about a space.

items.description: One word of the axis.

id.description: The word, for example component.

description.description: What the word means for a space.

options.description: The words a use case may use on this axis.

scope-question.description: A scope question: one of the five methods.

id.description: Scope question id: <scope>.<method>.

description.description: What the question decides, for a person or an agent.

options.description: The possible answers. Answers are semantic words, never raw values.

method.description: Which of the five methods this question answers.
